_meta.what: Machine-written daily brief per channel plus a composite line, generated from the payloads this site already publishes. Written by a language model, not the author; measurement language enforced by prompt and lint.
_meta.citation: Krishna, Ishan (2026). India Geopolitical Risk Monitor. https://igrm.in/

composite: The composite salience index printed 48.9 on 2026-08-06, held up by Gulf and shipping coverage at 77.7 and 80.9 while China and US trade attention sat far below their seven-day means, with the stress gauge at 65.7.

channels.pakistan_west: Pakistan and Western Border scored 65.1, some 23.8 points under its seven-day average of 88.9, across 56 articles with a tier-1/2 share of just 5.4 percent. Coverage clustered on Indus water sharing claims, Pakistani artillery acquisitions from China, and the PoK vote and related protests, none of it carried by top-tier outlets.
channels.china_east: China and Eastern Border registered 5.3, down 24.6 points from its seven-day average of 29.9. Evidence is thin: 14 articles, 14.3 percent tier-1/2, with only stalled border trade over a tax row and Tibet heritage reporting recurring, and no single dominant story.
channels.gulf_energy: Gulf and Energy Security scored 77.7, effectively flat against its seven-day average of 77.3, on 150 articles with an unusually high tier-1/2 share of 84 percent. Attention concentrated on reporting that a US-Iran Strait of Hormuz arrangement is close, Iranian signalling on talks, and Israeli casualties in Lebanon.
channels.us_trade: US and Trade Policy scored 15.6, 7.4 points below its seven-day average of 23.0, from 83 articles at 18.1 percent tier-1/2. The visible items were immigration-adjacent rather than trade-led: falling F-1 visa issuance to Indian and Chinese students, tighter USCIS rules, and a domestic political row over opening digital payments to US firms.
channels.shipping: Shipping and Chokepoints scored 80.9, down 7.6 points from its seven-day average of 88.5, on 150 articles with a 10 percent tier-1/2 share. The volume came almost entirely from Hormuz deal coverage, including the reported inbound-traffic terms and crude slipping below 80 dollars on the Iran-Oman track.
